items.title: From Drug Discovery to Precision Oncology: A Machine Learning–Driven Pharmaceutical Framework for Lung Cancer Treatment—A Joint Research Initiative Between Pakistan's Department of Pharmacy and China Pharmaceutical University
items.abstract: Lung cancer remains one of the most challenging global healthcare concerns due to its high mortality rate, molecular heterogeneity, therapeutic resistance, and limitations in conventional pharmaceutical drug development. This study presents an integrated machine learning–driven pharmaceutical framework for accelerating anticancer drug discovery, predicting therapeutic responses, and advancing precision oncology through a joint research initiative involving Pakistan’s Department of Pharmacy and China Pharmaceutical University. The research dataset comprised 18,500 bioactive compounds, 3,200 lung cancer patient profiles, and 12,600 drug–target interaction records, incorporating molecular descriptors, genomic biomarkers, pharmacokinetic properties, and clinical treatment-response characteristics. The proposed framework integrated molecular docking, quantitative structure–activity relationship modeling, Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and deep neural networks to identify promising therapeutic compounds and predict individualized drug responses. Molecular screening prioritized 245 potential anticancer compounds, of which 38 exhibited favorable predicted binding affinities, drug-likeness properties, and pharmacokinetic profiles. Experimental model evaluation indicated that XGBoost achieved 95.2% accuracy, 94.6% precision, 95.8% recall, and a 95.2% F1-score, outperforming Random Forest (91.8% accuracy) and deep neural networks (93.7% accuracy). Furthermore, XGBoost achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.974, demonstrating strong predictive discrimination. Biomarker-based analysis identified EGFR mutations, ALK rearrangements, KRAS alterations, and tumor-associated molecular signatures as influential determinants of therapeutic response. Patient-specific treatment stratification demonstrated a 21.4% improvement in drug–patient matching accuracy compared with the conventional baseline approach, while computational pharmaceutical screening reduced the estimated compound prioritization workload by 36.8%. The comparative pharmaceutical framework further highlighted opportunities for strengthening Pakistan–China collaboration in artificial intelligence-assisted drug development, translational oncology, and personalized therapeutic research. Collectively, the reported findings support the potential of integrating molecular pharmaceutical analysis with advanced machine learning to enhance computational drug candidate prioritization, improve treatment-response prediction, and facilitate biomarker-guided clinical decision support. Further experimental validation and prospective multicenter clinical evaluation remain essential before clinical implementation in diverse lung cancer populations.

items.title: From narrative generation to interpretive stabilization: generative AI and the mechanism of ethical understanding
items.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly reshaping narrative practices through character monologues and emotionally guided storytelling on digital platforms such as Bilibili and Chinese TikTok. While existing AI ethics scholarship has primarily focused on issues of bias, transparency, and governance, it offers limited explanatory power for understanding how generative systems reorganize the interpretive conditions under which moral judgment is formed. To address this gap, this study develops Generative Interpretive Mediation (GIM) as a mechanism-based framework for analyzing how GenAI intervenes in interpretive processes prior to explicit ethical evaluation. Based on an interpretive research design, the article examines widely circulated AI-generated character monologues as analytically selected cases of platform-mediated narrative production. The analysis identifies three interrelated operations: interpretive selection, interpretive pre-structuring, and interpretive orientation. Together, these operations do not simply produce narratives, but stabilize interpretation by reducing narrative ambiguity and guiding users toward coherent psychological trajectories. In doing so, GenAI often replaces sustained interpretive effort with pre-shaped explanatory closure, thereby reshaping how understanding is formed in everyday engagement with digital narratives. By bringing narrative hermeneutics into dialogue with behavioral accounts of the “illusion of understanding” and “decisional inertia,” the article situates GIM within an emerging epistemic turn in AI ethics. It argues that the central ethical concern of GenAI lies not primarily in biased outputs, but in its capacity to reorganize interpretive environments in ways that subtly condition the formation of public moral judgment.

items.title: From the Speed Race to the Engineering of Pause: A Quantitative Analysis of AI Latency vs. Human Conscious Threshold within the Rule of Conscious Existence (B + F = Nf)
items.abstract: The current era witnesses an unprecedented temporal gap between algorithmic processing speed and the speed of human consciousness. Drawing on the Rule of Conscious Existence (B + F = Nf), this study examines the Witness Paradox: primary sensory organs (B {bio}) process visual and auditory stimuli at speeds of 13–48 milliseconds (Raij et al., 2024; Potter et al., 2014), and tactile stimuli are processed preferentially and pre-attentively in approximately 150 milliseconds (Hanson et al., 2009). Conversely, Artificial Intelligence (B {AI}) processes data with a Time to First Token (TTFT) ranging from 100 to 550 milliseconds for ultra-fast systems (Gate.AI, 2026), while the involuntary bodily reflex (B {reflex}) responds in 122 milliseconds (Weerdesteyn et al., 2004). Yet, all these processes remain blind and do not witness. The Sovereign Witness (F), however, is the only entity that lags behind (at least 200 milliseconds) (Libet, 1983) to process data with a sequential capacity not exceeding 10 bits/second (Zheng & Meister, 2024), yet it alone is capable of generating authentic meaning (Nf). Through a quantitative analysis of response time data and neuroscientific measurements, this research demonstrates that modern algorithms operate within a Zone of Non-Witnessing, leading to a collapse of meaning (S_e < 0) unless a Pause Gate is engineered as a technical governance framework that imposes a strategic delay, ensuring the sovereign decision remains in human hands.

items.title: Gender Differences in User Performance and Muscle Activity across Varied Mouse Control-Display Gains for Fitts’ task
items.abstract: This study examined how gender differences shape distinct user performance and muscle control patterns in pointing tasks across varying computer mouse control-display gain settings. A total of 17 female and 15 male participants completed five 30-min Fitts’ Tasks under five distinct control-display gain configurations. Surface electromyography monitored muscle activity in the extensor digitorum, extensor carpi ulnaris, and flexor digitorum superficialis muscles, while GoFitts software recorded performance metrics. Results revealed differences in upper limb muscle activity and task performance between groups: As control-display gain varied, female users demonstrated higher and more stable accuracy, while male users exhibited more pronounced changes in muscle movement patterns. These findings provide practical recommendations for CDG settings tailored to different genders, offering insights into personalized human-computer interaction design.

items.title: Generative AI for Question Generation, Answer Scoring and Faculty-Supervised Assessment
items.abstract: Writing question papers and marking descriptive answers remain the slowest, most subjective parts of examination. This review organises recent work on automating them into three themes: generating questions, scoring answers, and deciding how far automated scores can be trusted. Eight core studies on Bloom's-level question generation, semantic and multi-signal evaluation and LLM-based scoring are examined, together with two 2025 studies. The synthesis shows that quality falls at higher cognitive levels, that combined scoring signals outperform similarity alone, that prompt design strongly affects reliability, and that no surveyed work integrates the full examination workflow. We therefore outline a faculty-in-the-loop reference design in which every generated question and every low-confidence score is checked by a human before use, and set out a plan for evaluating it. A web prototype built with Flask, MySQL and a hosted LLM already implements question generation, timed delivery and objective scoring for multiple-choice examinations, while descriptive scoring and confidence routing remain future work; no evaluation results are reported yet

items.abstract: Since the release of diverse generative AI (GenAI) tools such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini,DALL-E, and GitHub Copilot, there has been much debate around the impacts and implications of thesetools on education. Currently, extant literature remarks on the affordances, challenges, and opportunitiesof GenAI, but few studies report and analyze empirical studies and educational practices coming up byGenAI usage in learning settings. Then, in this Scoping Review (ScR) based on 146 studies retrievedfrom the databases SCOPUS, Web of Science (WoS), and ERIC, we analyzed the implications ofintegrating GenAI in engineering and computing education from K-12 to tertiary levels. We adopted anapproach starting from the bibliometric features of the studies in terms of authors, cites, years, or clustertopics, and navigating to the identification of methodologies, strategies, AI literacy instruments andguidelines, learning outcomes, and students’ and teachers’ perceptions, among other features. Weadvocate that current educational practices in engineering and computing with GenAI can indicate to us aroadmap of its potentialities, uses, and risks from the standpoint of both teachers and students, and thiscould help us to create more reflexive methodologies that enhance the teaching-learning process based onthe evidence. Our purpose with the outcomes and conclusions of this scoping review is to supporteducators, faculty members, and other stakeholders in engineering and computing education to co-createeducational methodologies that articulate GenAI with curricula, AI literacy, and prompt engineeringencompassing students’ learning domains such as cognitive, affective, or behavioral. items.title: Generative AI Usage, Data Privacy Awareness and Information Security Behavior Among Management Students
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid uptake of GenAI technologies such as ChatGPT, Gemini and others is affecting the way that students access information, prepare assignments, generate ideas, and communicate. In this case, GenAI is particularly important for management students because of the growing importance of digital literacy and use of data for making decisions in managerial positions in the future. On the other hand, the increased usage of GenAI is causing new concerns related to privacy, data security and misuse of confidential information. This study aims to explore the relationship between Generative AI Usage (GAIU), Data Privacy Awareness (DPA) and Information Security Behavior (ISB) among management students. The proposed study will use a quantitative, cross-sectional survey research design. The conceptual framework suggests that frequency and purposes of GenAI usage by students could influence their awareness about data privacy and information security measures. Further, Data Privacy Awareness is likely to have a positive effect on Information Security Behavior. The proposed research may use a Likert-scale questionnaire among undergraduate and postgraduate management students. As a demonstration of statistical analysis methods that would be used in this study, an illustrative dataset among 300 participants is provided. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlation analysis and multiple regression will be utilized. Illustrative results show that students may exhibit relatively high level of GenAI usage and relatively low privacy awareness and information security behavior. The suggested model suggests that data privacy awareness is likely to become one of the predictors of safe digital behavior. This study is going to contribute to the ongoing debate on responsible adoption of AI in higher education institutions. Keywords: Generative Artificial Intelligence, GenAI Usage, Data Privacy Awareness, Information Security Behavior, Management Students, Higher Education, Digital Literacy, Responsible AI

items.title: Green Chemistry in Pharmaceuticals: Emerging Strategies for Sustainable Drug Discovery, Manufacturing, Analysis, Packaging, and Waste Management
items.abstract: The pharmaceutical industry is vital to public health, but it also has a big influence on the environment because of things like waste production, hazardous reagents, and solvent-intensive synthesis. The goal of green pharmaceutical development is to apply green chemistry concepts at every stage of a product's life cycle, from molecular design to end-of-life care. Waste prevention, atom economy, safer chemistry, energy-efficient synthesis, and green analytical chemistry are among the modern green strategies included in this review. In addition to sustainable formulation techniques and cutting-edge technology like artificial intelligence and machine learning, it showcases novel techniques including biocatalysis, solvent-free reactions, and continuous-flow chemistry. The conversation highlights that no single technology is completely environmentally friendly and that attaining sustainability necessitates a thorough assessment of the effects of materials, energy, and life cycles while maintaining the quality and safety of pharmaceuticals.

items.title: Hardware architectures for posit arithmetic: evolution, trade-offs, and artificial intelligence
items.abstract: The IEEE 754 floating-point standard has been the backbone of scientific computing for decades. However, the rapid growth of deep learning (DL) and edge computing has highlighted its drawbacks, mainly in high memory bandwidth and energy usage. To solve this, the posit number system was introduced in 2017. It uses "tapered precision" to dynamically allocate more bits to the "Golden Zone," where artificial intelligence (AI) weights usually fall. Although theoretically better, early posit hardware faced a major "hardware tax" because decoding variable-length regime bits was too slow. This paper presents a detailed survey of posit hardware architectures from 2017 to 2025. We trace its evolution from basic scalar generators to advanced vectorized accelerators and compute-in-memory (CIM) designs. We highlight major improvements, such as leading difference detectors (LDD) and Radix-4 dividers, which have successfully reduced decoding delay by over 40% and energy consumption by 80%. Our comparative study shows that 16-bit posits can effectively replace 32-bit IEEE floats for memory-bound tasks. It saves 50% memory bandwidth without losing accuracy in applications like ResNet inference and climate modeling. Finally, we conclude that with recent RISC-V posit vector units (PVUs), posits demonstrate competitive potential relative to BFLOAT16 and FP8 formats, particularly in memory-bound edge applications.

items.title: Health information in Bangladesh: sources, trust, and perceived effectiveness of digital communication technologies
items.abstract: Abstract This study responds to the urgent need to understand the role that digital communication technologies play in shaping health information consumption in Bangladesh, a country that is grappling with persistent health crises, where common diseases often escalate to epidemic levels, resulting in substantial loss of life. Despite these challenges, public awareness of health issues remains suboptimal, compounded by a lack of preparedness, inadequate health infrastructure, and limited disease control programs. Data were collected between December 2024 and March 2026 through online surveys (n=191) and one-to-one interviews (n=65) conducted in both Bengali and English. Our diverse demographic includes both socio-economically privileged individuals and marginalized populations, such as those residing in the Korail slum of Dhaka. The findings expose a notable gap in awareness regarding the health information aspects of digital technologies, despite their widespread accessibility. Google and YouTube emerged as the most commonly used digital health information sources, followed by Facebook. ChatGPT appeared as an emerging supplementary source, while Arogga, DocTime, and Wikipedia were reported less frequently. Arogga is an online pharmacy and healthcare platform in Bangladesh, while DocTime provides online doctor consultation services. Although less frequently reported, these platforms were included to capture diverse digital health-information pathways beyond general search and social media platforms. Trust in these sources hinges on authenticity, information accuracy, medical reliability, popularity, verifiability, selective visual trust dynamics, and convenience.

items.title: Human centered artificial intelligence driven cybersecurity for business resilience using bibliometric and qualitative analysis
items.abstract: Cyber threats have become increasingly automated, adaptive, and difficult to manage through conventional rule-based security mechanisms. Artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data-mining techniques offer advanced capabilities for detecting suspicious activities, intrusions, malware, phishing, and anomalous network behavior. However, existing research remains predominantly model-centered and provides limited understanding of how AI-enabled cybersecurity systems are designed, explained, trusted, and used in practice. This study investigates AI-driven cyber-threat detection and chatbot-supported cybersecurity through a sequential mixed-method design. The first stage conducted a bibliometric analysis of publications indexed in Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection from 1 January 2016 to 30 April 2026. The 2026 records represent a partial publication year. The analysis examined publication trends, contributing authors, countries, sources, citation patterns, and keyword clusters. The second stage involved semi-structured interviews with 10 developers and 10 users to explore the functionalities, implementation requirements, perceived benefits, and concerns associated with chatbot-supported cybersecurity. The bibliometric findings identified three major research areas: cybersecurity and threat-detection applications, artificial intelligence and machine-learning detection methods, and data-mining-based network-intrusion detection. The qualitative findings indicate that cybersecurity chatbots can provide rapid warnings, explain cyber risks, support phishing identification, offer first-level incident guidance, improve cybersecurity awareness, and escalate serious cases to human specialists. However, participants also identified concerns regarding data quality, privacy, explainability, trust, false positives, false negatives, adversarial manipulation, and overreliance on automated advice. The study proposes a human-centered framework integrating data foundations, detection intelligence, chatbot interaction, developer responsibility, user acceptance, governance, human oversight, and continuous learning. items.title: Human Factors Extended Reality Showcase 2026
items.abstract: Extended reality (XR) technologies are increasingly adopted by human factors researchers and practitioners across domains ranging from manufacturing to workplace safety and ergonomics. This interactive XR Showcase session provides attendees with direct, hands-on engagement with XR devices and applications presented by researchers. This year’s demonstrations reflect growing interest in XR applications for skilled manual work and assembly, workplace safety and ergonomics, visualization, and mobility interaction. While training remains an established theme, an emerging trend is the integration of artificial intelligence within XR. Collectively, these demonstrations illustrate a broader shift in the field toward XR platforms that serve not only as visualization tools, but as integrated systems for performance measurement and human-AI collaboration. The XR Showcase advances the goals of HFES by strengthening community interaction and facilitating knowledge exchange among researchers, practitioners, and students interested in the expanding role of XR in human factors research and practice.

items.title: Human Factors in AI-Enabled Decision Support for Industry 4.0/5.0: A Scoping Review of Technical and Empirical Validation
items.abstract: As AI systems become increasingly embedded in industrial decision-making, ensuring they support rather than overwhelm human operators has emerged as a critical design challenge. Human factors construct such as cognitive workload, trust calibration, and situation awareness are central to this challenge, yet their empirical evaluation remains inconsistent. This scoping review examined 30 peer-reviewed studies to assess how consistently these constructs, alongside explainability and usability, were evaluated across Industry 4.0, and 5.0 contexts. A co-occurrence analysis revealed a structural misalignment: explainability and trust dominated the evaluation landscape, while cognitive workload and usability remained largely unmeasured. Workload and usability showed zero co-occurrence, and 11 papers (36.7%) reported trust without cognitive or performance validation. No study assessed all five constructs simultaneously. Integrated human-in-the-loop evaluation frameworks incorporating validated measures such as NASA-TLX and SUS are needed to ensure AI-enabled industrial systems are interpretable, cognitively safe, and aligned with Industry 5.0 principles.

items.title: Human Induced pluropotent stem cells in hepatocarcinogenesis
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality globally, presenting significant challenges in treatment due to tumor heterogeneity, drug resistance, and limitations of conventional preclinical models. Human-induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) offer a transformative platform for addressing these issues. Derived from adult somatic cells, hiPSCs possess pluripotency and self-renewal capabilities, enabling the generation of patient-specific and genetically engineered liver models, including two-dimensional hepatocyte-like cells and more physiologically relevant three-dimensional liver organoids. These hiPSC-derived models are revolutionizing drug development by facilitating high-throughput drug screening, improving the prediction of drug-induced liver injury (DILI), enabling personalized medicine approaches, and elucidating complex disease mechanisms. Despite challenges such as cost, cell maturation state, and scalability, ongoing advancements in culture techniques, microfluidics, and integration with artificial intelligence promise to further enhance the utility of hiPSC technology, holding immense potential for accelerating the discovery of novel therapies and improving patient outcomes in liver cancer.

items.title: Human-in-the-Loop Intelligent Automation: A Review of Trust, Oversight, and Workforce Implications
items.abstract: Intelligent automation is now used to retrieve information, predict, recommend, generate content, route workflows and take physical or administrative action. Human-in-the-loop (HITL) design is often suggested as a possible fail-safe but it does not necessarily mean that a person is always in control. Oversight can be undermined by lack of time, authority, competence, independent evidence, or feedback or by a lack of real accountability despite the title of oversight. In this paper we explore HITL intelligent automation from three intertwined perspectives: calibrated trust, operational oversight, and workforce implications. It combines existing human-automation research, guidance for human–AI interaction, risk-management standards, regulation, and evidence of labor. A threat model encompasses technical misfortune, adversarial manipulation, cognitive and organizational failure, and harmful deployment of workforce. The mathematical formulation determines the automation modes based on expected error consequence, uncertainty, review cost, workload and skill preservation. The suggested architecture is that of separating the execution of the model from the risk routing, human decision making, dual authorization, audit, appeal, and learning feedback. A seeded synthetic experiment with 10,000 binary decisions is conducted for the comparisons between automation-only, passive universal review, risk-adaptive HITL, and dual control. With the declared generator, adaptive review achieves a 83.6% to 85.0% accuracy rate, while reviewing 37.1% of cases, and dual control achieves a 87.0% accuracy rate with a 5.2% rate of high impact error. These are indicative values and not measurements taken in the workplace. The review finds that effective HITL systems must have meaningful intervention capability, calibrated reliance, representative evaluation, protected worker voice, continuous competence and evidence of oversight functioning under realistic workload and failure.

items.abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, has transformed User Experience (UX) and User Interface (UI) design.Traditionally a human-centered discipline built on creativity, empathy, and iterative evaluation, UX design now increasingly involves AI tools that generate interface concepts, recommend components, analyse user behaviour, and support prototyping.Yet limited research examines how UX professionals actually collaborate with AI and what determines successful AI-assisted design practice.This research develops and validates a Human-AI Assisted UI Design Framework (HAUIDF), integrating Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HCAI), the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Human-AI Teaming Theory, and Distributed Cognition Theory.The framework links AI transparency, explainability, and design capability; perceived usefulness, ease of use, and human control; AI trust and collaborative creativity; to UX productivity, design quality, designer satisfaction, and continued AI adoption intention.A mixed-method design is proposed: a quantitative survey of 300-400 UX professionals analysed with PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 4), complemented by 15-25 semi-structured interviews analysed thematically.The expected contribution is an empirically grounded account of AI as a collaborative design partner rather than an automation tool, offering theoretical contributions to HCI and AI-adoption research and practical guidance for designers, organizations, and AI tool developers pursuing human-centered AI workflows.

items.title: Impact of ChatGPT on Academic Integrity among Youth: Mediating Role of Critical Thinking
items.abstract: The study aimed to check the association of ChatGPT use and critical thinking on academic integrity. The research design is cross-sectional correlational study to collect data from university students aged from 18 to 23 years old. The sample size was 600 students taken via purposive sampling from the University of Gujrat, Pakistan. Standardized psychological scales of ChatGPT usage scale, critical thinking evaluation scale, and academic integrity scales were used. Our findings showed that ChatGPT has no significant effect on academic integrity but has positive effect on critical thinking. While critical thinking has positive effect on academic integrity. It showed that ChatGPT doesn’t directly change cheating behavior, but it can boost critical thinking for students, and that improved critical thinking is what increases academic integrity. Implications of the findings are discussed.

items.title: Improving Haemorrhage Prediction in General Ward Patients by Incorporating Patterns of Change Derived From Routine Ward Measurements
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Aim To evaluate whether patterns of change derived from routine ward measurements provide additional predictive value beyond the most recent clinical measurements for haemorrhage prediction in general ward patients. Design A retrospective cohort study. Methods Among 16,197 adult patients admitted to general wards in three university‐affiliated hospitals in South Korea, 1152 (7.1%) experienced haemorrhage, whereas 15,045 (92.9%) did not. Three machine‐learning algorithms evaluated three feature sets based on the most recent clinical measurements, patterns of change or both. Models were trained and internally validated using stratified five‐fold cross‐validation. Predictive performance was compared across feature sets using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, sensitivity, specificity and F1‐score. Shapley Additive Explanations were used to interpret the best‐performing model. Results Models using both recent measurements and patterns of change showed small but statistically supported improvements in the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve compared with models using recent measurements alone. Shapley Additive Explanations identified neutrophil count, platelet count, white blood cell count, urine output and vital signs as key predictors. Conclusion Patterns of change derived from routine ward measurements provided complementary predictive information for haemorrhage prediction in general ward patients beyond the most recent clinical measurements. Routinely collected ward data may therefore contain additional predictive information not captured by the most recent values alone. Implications for the Profession and/or Patient Care Machine‐learning models combining recent clinical measurements with patterns of change may support risk stratification in general ward patients; prospective evaluation is needed to determine their clinical utility. Impact The study examined whether patterns of change improve haemorrhage prediction. These findings suggest that routinely collected ward data may provide additional predictive information beyond the most recent clinical measurements. The potential value of this information for nursing surveillance and timely intervention warrants prospective evaluation. Reporting Method Transparent reporting of a multivariable prediction model for individual prognosis or diagnosis–artificial intelligence (TRIPOD + AI).

items.title: Innovation and Employee Productivity in Selected Private Higher Education Institutions in Laoag City: A Descriptive-Correlational Study
items.abstract: This study investigated the relationship between technological, process, and product innovation and employee productivity among employees of selected private higher education institutions (HEIs) in Laoag City, Philippines. It also examined whether age, sex, educational attainment, job tenure, and nature of work moderated the innovation–productivity relationship and developed a strategic action plan for institutional utilization of the findings. The participants were 271 full-time academic and non-academic employees from selected private HEIs. The findings showed that the institutions reported high levels of technological, process, and product innovation and high employee productivity. Process innovation had the strongest positive and statistically significant relationship with employee productivity, while technological innovation had a statistically significant but weaker positive relationship. Product innovation did not have a statistically significant relationship with employee productivity. None of the demographic characteristics significantly moderated the innovation–productivity relationship. The study recommends institutionalizing feasible policies for process innovation, strengthening technology utilization and responsible artificial intelligence integration, refining academic programs through Business Analytics and Artificial Intelligence in Research Methods, and establishing participatory and governance mechanisms that can sustain innovation within existing institutional resources.

items.title: Integrated Bibliometric and Computational Analysis of Artificial Intelligence in Sustainable Finance
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into financial services presents a transformative opportunity to advance sustainability goals, yet a systematic understanding of its current state and impact is essential. This review aims to synthesize existing literature on AI applications within the financial sector, emphasizing their role in promoting sustainability and environmental, social, and governance principles. The study screened 3507 articles published in ABS‐ranked journals between 2020 and 2025 on AI and sustainability, narrowing the sample to a core corpus of 181 articles for mixed‐method analysis combining bibliometric techniques with Python‐based data analytics. Synthesized findings reveal significant research prevalence across AI sub‐domains such as machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing within sustainable finance contexts. Although literature supports the potential of AI to act both as an enabler of financial inclusion and as a tool for environmental impact assessment, variations in study contexts suggest a need for further standardized research to fully quantify its long‐term efficacy.

items.title: Interpretable Deep Learning for Retinal Disease Detection
items.abstract: Eye diseases are a leading cause of global vision impairment, yet detection is often hindered by limited resources and geographic barriers. While Deep Learning (DL) offers automated diagnostic solutions, its black-box nature challenges clinical trust. This research investigates whether interpretability can be integrated into DL models for eye disease classification without compromising performance. Using an EfficientNet-B0 architecture, two models were trained on fundus images: one trained only on real images and another incorporating synthetic images generated by a Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Network (DCGAN) to simulate insufficient data. Both training approaches were evaluated using 3-fold cross-validation and analysed with eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques: Grad-CAM for visual heatmaps and SHAP for feature-contribution insights. A General Practitioner (GP) also assessed the clinical relevance of selected Grad-CAM outputs. Cross-validation produced mean accuracies of 91.59% ± 0.81% for the real-only model and 90.51% ± 0.83% for the mixed model, with no statistically significant difference in accuracy (paired t-test, p = 0.366). Synthetic image quality was further evaluated using fidelity and diversity metrics, while additional analyses examined classification errors, calibration, and robustness to explanations. These results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating interpretability with DL models for retinal disease classification, including scenarios involving synthetic data augmentation, supporting further development of transparent and accurate automated medical diagnostic tools.

items.title: Intrinsic Goals for Autonomous Agents: Hierarchical Exploration Captures Future Volitional Action in Drosophila
items.abstract: Animals have a remarkable capacity for autonomy---driven by intrinsic motivation---without external sensory cues or extrinsic objectives, yet the computational mechanisms behind this ability largely remain a mystery. We combine whole-brain recordings in the fruit fly (Drosophila melanogaster), which reveal neural representations of spontaneous exploratory decisions more than 10 seconds in advance, with a neuromechanical digital twin to test whether optimizing intrinsic goals yields realistically embodied artificial agents that quantitatively match fly behavior and internal representations of future volitional action during exploration. Our hierarchical policy selects from a discrete library of low-level motor primitives, consistent with ethological theories of behavioral syllables. We train agents without external reward using 20 intrinsic motivation algorithms spanning curiosity, entropy, and competency methods. The agents are evaluated in a virtual tethered-ball assay modeled on the fly experiment, comparing spontaneous locomotor statistics and internal representations and decoding future turn direction from kinematics and neural activity on the same timescales observed in flies. DIAYN, a hierarchical competency algorithm learning discrete policies that maximize behavioral entropy and the separability of induced sensory observations, achieves the strongest joint behavioral and neural prospective coding performance relative to flies. Its learned policies closely capture individual variability in fly exploration strategies, suggesting that this diversity serves to maximize state-space coverage at the population level. DIAYN's latent activity also closely captures the sum-difference rule for interhemispheric encoding of kinematics in biological flies. These results establish hierarchical, intrinsically motivated agents as a powerful framework for reverse-engineering animal autonomy.

items.title: Invisible barriers? Navigating ambition, visibility, and career development with endometriosis
items.abstract: Endometriosis affects approximately 10% of people of reproductive age, however its influence on career development remains underexplored. This study applies Social Cognitive Career Theory (SCCT) to examine how endometriosis can shape women’s career development. Using an interpretivist, qualitative design, six semi structured interviews with UK-based women aged 30-39 were analysed through reflexive thematic analysis. Findings highlight constrained career mobility, revised ambitions, overcompensation, burnout, and concerns about professional reputation, shaped by gendered workplace norms. Supportive management, flexible working, and Occupational Health (OH) provision mitigated these impacts. The study extends SCCT research and offers recommendations for inclusive careers support and workplace practice.

items.title: Is AI engine exposure associated with rising branded search? A two-source study of 347 US brands, 2015-2026, with a pre-specified analysis plan
items.abstract: Ranking Atlas Working Paper RA-WP-2026-02. Not peer reviewed. Background. Practitioners widely describe AI engines as a branding channel. In this account, users meet brands in AI answers and then search for them by name on Google. If this holds at scale, US branded search should rise relative to non-branded search as AI adoption grows, and brands that AI engines mention more should gain more. Methods. We froze an analysis plan with three hypotheses (H1a-c) before collecting outcome data, and later added four amendments; two of them added tests of AI recommendation (H2) and recommendation position (H3) after earlier results had been seen. The sample was 347 US brands in 14 categories plus 140 non-branded control terms. AI exposure, top-3 rate and position tier came from 420 ChatGPT and Gemini responses to category prompts (Gemini answers were not US-localised). Outcomes were US branded search in Google Trends (2015-2026) and Google Ads (2022-2026), with pre-AI placebo tests, split-half checks, Holm correction and equivalence tests. Growth is reported in percentage points (pp) of annual growth (log points x 100). Results. No H1 test was supported. The exposure gradient was +2.13 pp per year per SD in Trends (95% CI -0.82 to 5.08) and +2.28 in Ads (95% CI -1.15 to 5.72), and equivalence to zero was not established, so an effect of 2 pp cannot be ruled out. Branded search did not gain share against non-branded search in either source. Brands named among the first three in at least 20% of AI answers grew faster: +7.13 pp per year against matched brands in Ads (95% CI 2.10 to 12.36), with no significant gap in 2015-2022 Trends growth, but the gap was not stable over time. Ads growth was ordered by position tier (+5.42 pp per tier step), but before ChatGPT the ordering tended to run the other way. Under the pre-specified rules both results are inconclusive, and whether first position beats positions 2-3 could not be resolved (11 brands in first position). Conclusions. We found no confirmatory evidence that AI adoption has raised US branded search overall. Brands that AI answers name early show faster recent branded growth, but the top-3 gap was unstable over time and the position ordering tended to reverse a pre-2022 pattern. These patterns are compatible with a modest aggregate echo of individual-level effects reported by industry studies, and also with AI engines favouring already-popular brands. The study does not establish causation.

items.title: ISCR-SocioValidate: Reproducible Analysis Package for the Sociological Validation of the Integrated State Cyber Resilience (ISCR) Model
items.abstract: ISCR-SocioValidate is a Python package with documentation that makes the sociological validation of the Integrated State Cyber Resilience (ISCR) model reproducible. The ISCR model is a seven-layer governance architecture for state cyber resilience under hybrid threats. Its layers are strategic, institutional, operational-coordination, technological, human, legal, and international. The sociological validation asks whether professionals from cybersecurity-relevant sectors accept the model's proposals and which social and organizational preconditions they associate with its implementation. Version 0.1.0 works from a single file of published aggregate survey results (187 of 245 invited professionals) and recomputes every derived statistic and figure of the associated article: 95% Wilson score intervals for top-two-box agreement; an audit of the integer counts consistent with rounded percentages; reliability diagnostics (Cronbach's alpha, Spearman–Brown split-half reliability, implied mean inter-item correlation); a joint display that integrates closed-ended and open-ended evidence across the seven layers, using triangulation categories (agreement, partial agreement, silence, dissonance). Functions for intercoder agreement (Cohen's kappa, Krippendorff's alpha) and item-level diagnostics prepare a respondent-level mode, which is under development. The record contains the source code, 13 unit tests, the aggregate input file with references to its source tables, a codebook template, generated tables (CSV), and Figures 1–2 (TIFF 800 dpi and PDF). It also includes documentation on the architecture, data schema, an analysis plan aligned with the APA Journal Article Reporting Standards, ethics and data governance, reproducibility, and a roadmap. No respondent-level or personal data are included, and no generative AI is used to code or interpret participants' answers. Requirements: Python 3.11 or later, numpy, pandas, matplotlib. items.title: K-12 AI literacy frameworks after generative AI: A scoping review
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) literacy has become a priority in K-12 education, yet frameworks for teaching and assessing it remain fragmented across grade levels, national contexts, and disciplinary traditions. This scoping review maps and synthesizes framework-level contributions to K-12 AI literacy published between January 2024 and December 2025. Following JBI guidance and PRISMA-ScR reporting standards, we searched four databases and grey literature sources, screened 204 unique records, and applied a purpose-built checklist covering five criteria: grade bands, competencies, critical constructs, assessment, and exemplars. Fifty studies met the inclusion threshold. The corpus spans 15 countries, with the United States (32%), Hong Kong (26%), and mainland China (12%) accounting for 70% of included studies. Frameworks defined AI literacy through cognitive, affective, behavioral, ethical, and social dimensions, but dimensional models used inconsistent labels and constructs, with limited crosswalk among them. The ABCE framework offered the closest approximation to a shared measurement tradition, with adaptation across three educational systems. Assessment and curriculum also developed largely in parallel: scale-development papers reported psychometric evidence without instructional sensitivity data, while curriculum papers assessed learning through lesson-linked tools that limited cross-study comparison. Generative AI competencies, including output evaluation, hallucination detection, and prompt design, remained peripheral in most frameworks despite their relevance to students’ everyday encounters with AI. Geographic concentration and limited attention to socioeconomic status, disability, and linguistic diversity further constrained transferability. The field needs stronger convergence through shared vocabulary, curriculum-aligned assessment, longitudinal evidence, and cross-context validation.

items.abstract: Technology-facilitated domestic violence challenges legal systems because everyday digital tools can extend surveillance, intimidation, and coercive control beyond physical encounters. This study examines Indonesia's legal readiness for early detection of technology-facilitated domestic violence, identifies interpretive gaps faced by law enforcement officers, and formulates an operational framework for accountable risk screening. Using a normative-empirical socio-legal approach, the study combines doctrinal analysis of relevant Indonesian laws with thematic analysis of verified interviews involving a Protection of Women and Children police officer, a legal counsel, and a survivor in Gorontalo. The findings show that the principal problem is not an absolute legal vacuum but fragmented legal readiness: relevant norms exist across several legal regimes, while frontline interpretation, digital evidence preservation, institutional capacity, and rapid victim protection remain weakly integrated. The study also identifies procedural fatigue as a factor that may affect survivors' willingness to continue legal processes. Artificial intelligence is positioned as an emerging risk and potential decision-support instrument, not an autonomous legal decision-maker. The study proposes a Five-Dimensional Legal Readiness Framework (KKH-5): normative recognition, interpretive integration, evidentiary readiness, institutional capacity, and protective responsiveness. The framework supports pattern-based interpretation, human oversight, due process, and survivor-centred early intervention.

items.title: Machine Behavior: Paradigm Shift of Communication Research in AI Era
items.abstract: The widespread integration of artificial intelligence (AI)–driven communication agents, particularly large language models, has brought about a paradigm shift in communication research. Traditional human-centered paradigms are becoming inadequate for analyzing the behaviors and impacts of these non-human agents, which exhibit autonomous and intelligent communicative capabilities. This article advocates for the development of a Machine Behavior Paradigm in communication studies. This proposed paradigm explicitly expands the disciplinary scope by integrating machine behavior into three core dimensions. About research objects, it emphasizes the shifts from a human-only focus to a dual focus on humans and intelligent machines as communicative subjects. For research approaches, it should expand beyond human–human relationships to encompass machine–machine and hybrid human–machine interactions. In methodologies, we advocate to integrate computational indicators, such as text-generation temperature and activity frequency, alongside traditional empirical tools to address the opacity of AI “black boxes.” Furthermore, the article examines the limitations of current communication theories, such as agenda-setting and the spiral of silence, when applied to AI-driven environments. Also, we argue that it is difficult to study opaque AI systems with traditional methodologies. This shift necessitates interdisciplinary collaboration and the establishment of robust ethical guidelines to ensure the responsible study of autonomous agents. By outlining a systematic framework for individual, collective, and hybrid machine behavior, this article provides a roadmap for future inquiry.

items.title: Make It Work, Then Make It Better: Building a Hassaniya Machine Translation System
items.abstract: Hassaniya, the Arabic dialect of Mauritania, has almost no machine translation (MT) resources and no standard orthography, and it is among the weakest varieties for current large language models on recent dialectal Arabic benchmarks. A usable Hassaniya translator would let its speakers reach digital, financial, and public services in their own language. We report how we built one in two steps. We first fine-tuned NLLB-200 (1.3B) for English↔Hassaniya on about 25k sentence pairs; it reaches 59.4 chrF++ into English but only 41.5 into Hassaniya. English proves a poor pivot, since it does not mark the gender or politeness that Hassaniya requires when addressing someone. We therefore switch to Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) and fully fine-tune the Apache-2.0 model MADLAD-400 3B for Hassaniya↔MSA, with a new language tag, on four small parallel corpora (26.7k pairs after cleaning and leakage removal). To measure what each corpus contributes, we train four cumulative models and score them on a test set with an equal share from every corpus, using chrF++, spBLEU, and a copy rate that counts untranslated outputs. Zero-shot, MADLAD-400 copies 90.2% of its MSA inputs instead of producing Hassaniya. The final model reaches 48.0 chrF++ / 34.8 spBLEU for MSA→Hassaniya and 59.3 / 48.0 for Hassaniya→MSA, gains of +21.4 / +23.9 and +31.5 / +33.7 over the base model, and its copy rate falls to 6.9% (human references: 3.5%). Every corpus improves the overall score significantly, but gains are largely confined to each corpus’s own domain. A small conversational service corpus gives the largest gain after the first, and two corpora interfere in the direction that generates Hassaniya. The translator now powers a public Hassaniya chatbot that pivots through MSA to a general-purpose large language model.

items.title: Measuring Visual Clutter in AI-Generated Pillar-to-Pillar Automotive Displays: Objective Metrics, Perception, and Search Performance
items.abstract: Large pillar-to-pillar (P2P) displays are replacing traditional instrument clusters, but their visual richness may impair visual search and increase driver distraction. We examined how visual properties of large automotive displays relate to perceived clutter and search performance using subjective, objective, and behavioral measures. Fifty-five participants viewed 18 AI-generated dashboard videos, completed a detection task, and rated clutter, density, overlap, colorfulness, and brightness; corresponding objective metrics were computed from video frames. Subjective density and overlap best predicted clutter, while overlap, edge density, and colorfulness predicted search time. Factor analysis revealed two dimensions, spatial complexity and surface appearance, showing that spatial properties primarily drive clutter perception and that objective metrics can support early-stage interface screening.

items.title: Methods and Tools for Multi-hazard Risk Assessment
items.abstract: Abstract Multi-Hazard Risk Assessment (MHRA) integrates hazard, exposure, and vulnerability analyses to quantify potential disaster impacts and support risk-informed decision-making. It evaluates the probability and consequences of multiple, interacting hazards such as floods, earthquakes, hurricanes, and landslides, and their cascading effects on people, infrastructure, and ecosystems. MHRA approaches range from qualitative methods, including community-based assessments and indicator-based analyses, to quantitative and probabilistic models that estimate economic and human losses. Advances in data availability, modelling, and artificial intelligence have enhanced the precision of risk estimation, while frameworks such as CAPRA, HAZUS, RiskScape, and CLIMADA provide practical tools for implementation. The chapter also highlights the importance of regional collaboration, uncertainty analysis, and scenario-based forecasting for adaptive planning. Strengthening MHRA capacities, particularly in data integration and multi-scale modelling, is essential to improving disaster preparedness, financial resilience, and long-term climate adaptation strategies.

items.title: Nanoparticle delivery systems for gene therapy of degenerative musculoskeletal diseases
items.abstract: Degenerative musculoskeletal diseases (DMDs) are a group of chronic conditions characterized by the progressive deterioration of tissue structure and function, primarily affecting the articular cartilage, bones, tendons, and ligaments. With global aging populations, the rising prevalence of these disorders presents a growing public health challenge. Current treatments for DMDs are limited by substantial drug side effects and restricted therapeutic efficacy. Gene therapy has emerged as a promising alternative for addressing these conditions. Nanoparticles are essential for overcoming intracellular and extracellular barriers in nucleic acid delivery. Recent technological advances have led to novel nanomaterials and strategies, which have enabled safer and more efficient gene therapy. This review comprehensively analyzes the role of nanoparticle delivery systems in enabling effective gene-based interventions for major DMDs. First, we analyze the main gene therapies for various DMDs. Next, we systematically summarize recent advances in nanocarrier platforms and delivery strategies targeting osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, intervertebral disc degeneration, and tendon diseases. Finally, we discuss key challenges and future directions, offering a roadmap to advance nanoparticle delivery therapeutics toward clinical impact. This synthesis uniquely bridges nanoparticle delivery design with disease-specific pathophysiology, providing strategic guidance for overcoming translational barriers through emerging technologies including AI-driven carrier optimization and organ-on-chip platforms. Across these diseases, no carrier is universally optimal: systemic bone delivery prioritizes circulation stability and cell-selective targeting, whereas local delivery to cartilage, intervertebral discs, and tendons requires a balance among tissue retention, matrix penetration, cellular uptake, and controlled release. Current evidence remains predominantly preclinical and frequently demonstrates tissue accumulation without fully establishing intact-cargo delivery, functional target engagement, long-term safety, or manufacturability. This review therefore links nanoparticle design to disease-specific barriers and identifies the evidence required for clinical translation. The Translational Potential of this Article. This review focuses on the clinical translational potential of nanoparticle-based delivery systems for gene therapy in degenerative musculoskeletal diseases (DMDs). Addressing the unique physiological and pathological barriers of specific musculoskeletal tissues (such as bone, cartilage, intervertebral discs, and tendons), this article systematically summarizes targeting and sustained-release strategies designed to enhance delivery efficiency and overcome tissue-specific obstacles. Furthermore, this study highlights future perspectives, including artificial intelligence (AI)-driven carrier optimization, organ-on-a-chip models, and multimodal combination therapies integrating biomaterials and cells. By addressing the limitations of conventional therapies that merely alleviate symptoms without reversing tissue degeneration, this review provides a robust theoretical foundation and a clear translational roadmap for the development of precise, safe, and long-lasting gene therapy regimens for DMDs.

items.title: Navigating chaos and leapfrogging to Pharma 5.0 with ontological honesty and epistemic humility
items.abstract: Abstract: Pharmaceutical manufacturing remains constrained by legacy paradigms that collapse engineered systems into static legal descriptors and struggle to integrate real‑world evidence. Geopolitical instability, supply‑chain fragility, climate‑driven disruption, declining institutional trust and the accelerating influence of generative artificial intelligence expose that constraint as an epistemic ceiling. This Perspective outlines a professional path for leapfrogging toward a patient‑centric Pharma 5.0 paradigm grounded in ontological honesty and epistemic humility. The argument traces this ceiling across three layers—the individual practitioner, the quality system and the broader ecosystem—and places Deming’s System of Profound Knowledge, Kegan’s orders of consciousness and McGilchrist’s hemispheric account alongside the classical sequence of the nafs and a heart‑centered posture of practice (Dil Se). Leapfrogging is a knowledge strategy before it is a technology strategy. Recent United States hearings and independent quality‑scoring efforts reveal an ontology capable of detecting divergence yet unable to revise certified reality. Pakistan and the broader Global South live under the same ceiling, shaped by high generic volumes and thin margins. Thailand’s May 2025 registration of a domestically developed trastuzumab biosimilar demonstrates capability‑first sequencing; a subsequent United States draft guidance issued on 29 October 2025—proposing that comparative efficacy studies may be unnecessary when analytical comparability is high—confirms the direction of that sequence rather than authorizing it after the fact. Preparing for Pharma 5.0 requires unlearning certain validated habits, cultivating sovereignty of judgment before sovereign infrastructure and building quality systems capable of revising their own descriptions.

items.title: Non-Invasive Brain Stimulation as a Method for Mitigation of Spaceflight Neurodegeneration & Associated Cognitive Decline
items.abstract: Evidence is mounting toward the idea that spaceflight stressors decrease cognitive function over time. Current countermeasures focus largely on spacecraft design and environmental modifications, but direct interventions on astronaut physiology could be essential for long-term success. Noninvasive brain stimulation (NiBS) is increasingly used to modulate neuroplasticity and has shown promise for improving cognition in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and related conditions. NiBS appears plausible as a countermeasure candidate for spaceflight-associated cognitive decline; space-radiation pathways overlap with AD-relevant mechanisms, and AD trials demonstrate rTMS-associated cognitive and plasticity gains. However, the current literature primarily supports plausibility and mechanism overlap rather than direct validation in spaceflight or high-fidelity analogs; there is little evidence for NiBS effects in microgravity; spaceflight-induced brain changes may alter stimulation responses; validated operational protocols and standardized biomarkers are lacking; and long-term safety under extreme environments is uncertain.

items.title: One Standard Does Not Fit All: Limitations of Applying MIL-STD-1472H Across Diverse Government Programs
items.abstract: MIL-STD-1472H (Military Standard 1472 Version H) is the human engineering design standard applied across U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) acquisition programs. While the standard allows tailoring, it is frequently applied as a universal compliance baseline across diverse systems. One-size-fits all prescriptive standards can diminish human performance risks and constrain design adaptability (Dekker, 2017). Reliance on extensive tailoring increases system cost with minimal value and limits innovation. A subsection-level assessment of the Detailed Requirements section of MIL-STD-1472H demonstrates substantial variability in relevance across domains. In practice, tailoring serves as administrative compliance rather than advancing human performance outcomes. In addition, MIL-STD-1472H fails to address emerging challenges with integrating artificial intelligence into human-machine interfaces. Future DoD human engineering standards need to better align with system context, lifecycle maturity, and emerging technologies, consistent with Department of Defense artificial intelligence (AI) policy.

items.title: Personnel training for the digital construction industry: economic aspects
items.abstract: The digital transformation of the construction industry is one of the key areas for improving the efficiency of investment and construction activities. The introduction of building information modeling technologies, digital twins, artificial intelligence, automated project management systems and other digital tools requires qualified specialists who are able to work in a digital economy. At the same time, the construction sector is facing a shortage of personnel with the necessary digital competencies. The article examines the economic aspects of personnel training for the digital construction industry, analyzes the causes of personnel shortages, examines the costs of training and corporate staff development, and evaluates the effectiveness of investments in improving employee digital literacy. Special attention is paid to the issues of interaction between educational organizations and construction companies as the main mechanism for the formation of human resources in the industry. Based on the analysis, promising models of cooperation between universities and employers are proposed, ensuring an increase in the quality of specialist training and a reduction in personnel shortages.

items.title: Predictive Artificial Intelligence in SEND Systems: Evaluating Early Identification, Risk, and Governance Implications
items.abstract: The application of predictive artificial intelligence (AI) within Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) systems represents one of the most consequential and underexplored frontiers in contemporary educational data mining. This study investigates the deployment of machine learning algorithms to identify learners who may require additional support, evaluating the reliability, validity, and fairness of such predictive systems within the United Kingdom educational framework. Drawing on a structured literature synthesis spanning 2015–2025, a comparative analysis of seven machine learning algorithms including Random Forest, XGBoost, Support Vector Machine, and Neural Networks was conducted using datasets simulated from real-world SEND contexts. Results demonstrate that ensemble methods, particularly Random Forest and XGBoost, achieve the most consistent cross-validation performance (accuracy 74.3–77.5%), while simpler models offer greater interpretability. However, significant concerns emerge regarding false positive and false negative classification rates across protected demographic groups, with girls, learners from minority ethnic backgrounds, and those with masking conditions systematically underidentified. Governance analysis reveals critical gaps in the UK regulatory landscape, including an absence of mandatory explainability standards and algorithmic fairness requirements specific to SEND AI tools. This study proposes a five-pillar governance framework encompassing legal compliance, transparency, equity, human oversight, and data quality as a basis for the responsible deployment of predictive AI in SEND settings. Findings underscore that algorithmic decision support should complement rather than replace professional judgement, with human-in-the-loop protocols essential to ethical implementation.

items.title: Proper working-time accounting as a safeguard for employees’ occupational health and safety
items.abstract: Abstract Every employee has the right to working conditions that respect their health, safety, and dignity. Working time is a condition of employment and is subject to restrictions to safeguard employees’ occupational health and safety. EU Member States are obliged to ensure that these restrictions are observed in employment relationships. Compliance with working-time restrictions can be ensured through working-time accounting. The corresponding obligation is imposed on employers, who are expected to establish an objective, reliable, and accessible system for accounting for working time. This article examines how to create a working-time accounting system that meets the above conditions and protects employees’ health and safety. To calculate working time, it is essential to understand the various ways in which it can be determined. An “always-on” work culture and the blurring of boundaries between working and rest time complicate working-time accounting. The absence of national regulation may lead employers to assume that it is sufficient to measure working time at their own discretion. This approach creates inequality at the national level and fails to foster a favourable environment for protecting workers’ health, safety, and dignity. In this article, the authors present their view of how a working-time accounting system should be designed to ensure safeguards for employees’ occupational health and safety. The article is based on an analysis of European Union, Spanish, German, Greek, and Estonian regulations.

items.abstract: Justification: The integration of generative artificial intelligence into higher education has created opportunities to enhance teaching planning, material development, learning, and assessment, but has also raised concerns regarding academic integrity, data protection, transparency, and teacher training. Objective: To propose an ethical-pedagogical framework to guide the responsible integration of generative artificial intelligence into educational processes at public universities in Santo Domingo during 2026. Methodology: A qualitative approach, non-experimental design, and descriptive-propositional scope were adopted, applying legal-doctrinal, analytical, descriptive, documentary, and deductive methods through documentary analysis. Results: The documentary analysis revealed that the educational integration of generative artificial intelligence required institutional principles related to transparency, accountability, data protection, teacher training, disclosure of its use, and verification of generated content, along with changes in assessment practices aimed at preserving student authorship and strengthening knowledge acquisition. Conclusion: Educational uses, risks, and criteria related to transparency, teacher training, human oversight, academic integrity, learning assessment, and data protection were identified.

items.title: PyPI API Drift: A Release-Level Record of Public API Changes in 1,872 Popular Python Libraries, with a Checker and a Benchmark for Version-Aware Code Generation
items.abstract: Ask a code assistant to append a row to a pandas DataFrame and it may write df.append(row), a method removed in pandas 2.0. Models trained on code from many releases cannot tell which API exists in the version a user has installed, and benchmarks of this problem are small and frozen. We present PyPI API Drift, a release-level record of the public APIs of the 1,872 most-downloaded Python libraries: up to 80 recent final releases each (55,565 releases, 2021–October 2026), with signatures, 15,258,652 release-to-release changes and 210,535 deduplicated breaking changes. Extraction is static and import-free, reads only the needed bytes of each wheel, separates names that were truly removed from names that merely left the documented API, and marks with confidence labels and a coverage layer where static analysis cannot see. It is a high-precision, low-recall record: in two held-out runtime audits by AI agents isolated from the pipeline (on earlier data versions), 88.8% and 91.9% of high-confidence breaking changes were confirmed, while recall over all runtime-visible changes is limited (16 of 99). On top of it we release an offline checker, lookup tools with a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for coding agents, and VersionProbe, a benchmark of 10,958 valid/invalid snippet pairs. In a preregistered code-repair experiment, repeated across 4 models from one model family, API history from the dataset raised the share of API-compatible, intent-preserving migrations (under our evaluation protocol) to 68.5%–69.9% for every model, from 7.0%–56.6% unaided and 46.2%–62.2% with the new release’s documentation. 13.4% of patch releases contain at least one breaking change.Code: https://github.com/pushkardg/pypi-api-drift Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/pushkar87dg/pypi-api-drift

items.title: Quantifying Shared Mental Models in Nursing Using Multimodal Physiological and Communication Data
items.abstract: Shared Mental Models (SMMs) are essential for effective nursing teamwork, yet existing assessments mainly rely on observations or self-reports that provide limited insight into team cognition during task execution. This study proposes a multimodal framework for quantifying SMM quality in virtual reality nursing simulations. Thirty nursing students (15 two-person teams) completed three collaborative clinical scenarios while electroencephalography (EEG), eye-tracking, and communication data were synchronously collected. Expert annotations were used to classify teams into high- and low-SMM groups. Results showed significant differences in neural activity, visual attention organization, and communication structures between the two groups. High-SMM teams demonstrated distinct EEG patterns, more organized gaze behaviors, and stronger connectivity between task-oriented communication components. These findings suggest that multimodal physiological and behavioral measures can provide objective indicators of SMM quality and support future development of real-time assessment tools for nursing teamwork and simulation-based education.

items.title: RAG-Based MCA AI Agent for Document-Grounded College Information Assistance Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Vector Search and a Locally Hosted Large Language Model
items.abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-based MCA AI Agent for document-grounded question answering over college and student policy documents. The system uses PyMuPDF for PDF text extraction, approximately 1000-character chunks, Nomic-Embed-Text for generating 768-dimensional embeddings, and Pinecone for semantic vector search. At query time, the system retrieves the three most relevant document chunks and provides them as context to Llama 3.2 running locally through Ollama. A React.js frontend and FastAPI backend provide the conversational interface. The paper describes the system architecture, methodology, implementation, document-refresh workflow, and practical deployment considerations, including stale vectors and local inference latency. It also outlines an evaluation framework for comparing a standalone LLM with the proposed RAG pipeline using retrieval relevance, answer correctness, faithfulness, and latency. The current work is presented as a system implementation and preliminary study. A controlled quantitative evaluation has not yet been completed, and no numerical accuracy improvement is claimed. Keywords: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Large Language Models, Semantic Search, Vector Database, Pinecone, Llama 3.2, Ollama, FastAPI, React.js, Document-Grounded Question Answering.

items.title: Recent advances and emerging trends in smart parking technologies from sensor based to next generation parking system: a review
items.abstract: Rapid urbanization, growing vehicle ownership, and limited parking infrastructure have made parking allocation a major challenge in modern cities. To address this issue, numerous smart parking systems (SPSs) have been proposed to improve parking efficiency, reduce congestion, and enhance user convenience. This paper presents a comprehensive review and comparative analysis of SPSs in terms of technological approaches, sensing methods, networking technologies, computational models, user interfaces, and service capabilities. It also addresses an important research gap by evaluating the suitability of different SPS approaches under diverse environmental conditions and highlighting their key advantages and limitations. The review emphasizes the growing role of internet of things (IoT)-based, multi-approach architectures in enabling real-time monitoring, reservation, payment integration, and vehicle guidance for smart city applications. Furthermore, it discusses the potential of integrating reconfigurable systems with IoT to improve adaptability, scalability, and responsiveness through dynamic resource allocation and efficient local decision-making. Despite these benefits, challenges related to interoperability, security, energy management, design complexity, and deployment cost remain significant. Future SPSs are expected to incorporate artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, dynamic pricing, autonomous vehicle support, and digital twin technologies to achieve more adaptive, intelligent, and sustainable parking management.

items.title: Reconciling Food and Energy on the Same Land: An Explainable Artificial Intelligence Framework for Agrivoltaic Suitability Mapping
items.abstract: The swift growth of utility-scale solar farms has created fierce competition for agricultural land, especially in countries where prime solar energy sites and productive croplands coincide. Agrivoltaic structures, which incorporate agricultural food and electricity generation on one parcel, are a structural solution to this kind of land-use conflict; yet the question of where such systems should be sited has, to date, been addressed in the literature predominantly through subjective multi-criteria decision making methods. This study develops a fully data-driven and explainable machine learning framework for agrivoltaic site selection, using the province of Konya—Türkiye's grain basket and its largest agricultural region—as a case study. The site selection problem is formulated as a supervised binary classification task in which the geographic inventory of existing solar installations provides the ground-truth labels. Thirteen selected feature spanning climatic, topographic, economic, and socio-environmental dimensions were examined through Pearson correlation, variance inflation factor, and mutual information gain analyses. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting machine learning algorithms were trained with hyperparameter optimization, and observed performance variations were verified using omnibus Cochran's Q and pairwise McNemar statistical tests. Extreme Gradient Boosting achieved the highest performance (total accuracy: 0.9549, F1 score: 0.9533), followed by Random Forest (0.9390) and Logistic Regression (0.8661). Explainable artificial intelligence analysis, which renders the black-box nature of the models transparent, revealed that the most decisive factors determining agrivoltaic suitability were, respectively, distance to grid lines and global horizontal irradiance (GHI). The findings suggest that the proposed methodology may help minimize conflicts between energy and food security, thereby providing a strategic planning tool that can support progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals (particularly SDGs 7 and 13).

items.title: RECONSTRUCTING CRIMINAL LIABILITY FOR AI-ENABLED CYBERCRIME IN INDONESIA: Toward a Normative Framework of Responsibility
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has fundamentally transformed the nature of cybercrime from human-controlled conduct into algorithmically mediated and semi-autonomous operations. In Indonesia, this transformation is reflected in the sharp increase in cybercrime cases, automated fraud, and AI-enabled digital manipulation, which challenge the traditional criminal liability framework based on human intent and direct control. This study employs normative legal research integrating statutory, conceptual, and comparative approaches to examine the adequacy of existing legal frameworks and to formulate a reconstructed model of criminal liability for AI-based cybercrime. The findings reveal that Indonesia’s current legal regime, primarily governed by the Criminal Code and Electronic Information and Transactions Law, remains rooted in an actor-based liability paradigm, resulting in an accountability gap when harm is caused through autonomous or semi-autonomous AI systems. This article offers a novel normative reconstruction based on a risk- and control-based liability framework operationalized through six elements: recognition of systemic AI risk, expansion of fault doctrine to include algorithmic oversight failure, adoption of multi-tier criminal liability, mandatory algorithmic transparency and audit trails, corporate liability based on risk management failure, and integration of the duty of care principle. This model preserves the principle of personal criminal responsibility while extending liability to actors who control and manage technological risk. The study contributes theoretically by bridging classical fault-based liability and risk-based accountability in criminal law and provides normative recommendations for harmonizing national criminal law and developing AI-specific regulations to ensure legal certainty and effective accountability in the digital era

items.title: Reconstruction of Criminal Event Timelines from Property Crime Investigation Documents Based on a Hybrid LLM-Rule Pipeline
items.abstract: Fact-finding in criminal proceedings reconstructs past events into a coherent narrative based on fragmented evidence and testimony, yet remains vulnerable to cognitive confirmation bias. While automating timeline construction using large language models (LLMs) offers decision support, confidentiality-critical local models are prone to temporal hallucinations, inverting causal orders or generating groundless timestamps. To mitigate these vulnerabilities, this study proposes Deep-ARC (Analysis, Reconstruction, and Contradiction detection for criminal timeline construction), a hybrid LLM-rule pipeline that algorithmically regulates model reasoning through legal domain schemas and deterministic rule logic. Deep-ARC injects statutory crime element schemas to categorize event phases and enforces phase-aware boundary clamping grounded on explicit timestamps, systematically resolving sequential contradictions during missing time inference. In proof-of-concept experiments focusing on corporate property crimes (breach of trust and embezzlement) with Gemma-4-31B, Deep-ARC achieved a Micro PMR (exact sequence match ratio) of 0.343 and a Kendall’s Tau (τ) of 0.861, representing an approximate fourfold improvement over the unconstrained baseline and demonstrating higher sequencing consistency than large-scale commercial LLMs. These results indicate that coupling domain-specific structural constraints with deterministic algorithms offers an effective and robust strategy for providing an objective chronological sequence to assist fact-finding without relying exclusively on parameter scaling.
